title: Тост ученика и уксусный вкус  (The Pupil's Toast and the Vinegar Taste)

segments.t: In the dining room, before anyone takes a bite, Valdemar Barani raises a glass and announces to the press that this famous dish was actually invented by his teacher, Viktor Petrovich Barinov, to whom he owes everything. Overcome with guilt as the guests choke on the vinegar-soaked roll, Barani hands Barinov the keys to a brand-new car outside before rushing to the airport.
Господа, хочу сказать буквально пару слов.
Это блюдо в свое время придумал мой учитель.
Дорогие друзья, к сожалению, мне пора в аэропорт.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Господа, хочу сказать буквально пару слов.
'Gentlemen, I want to say literally a couple of words.' The grammar packs 'gentlemen' and 'of words' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Это блюдо в свое время придумал мой учитель.
'This dish was originally invented by my teacher.' Vika anchors the line on 'this', while 'teacher' completes the thought.
'Viktor Petrovich Barinov.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'Viktor' and 'Petrovich' in a few short words. Vika answers right away.
'The head chef of this restaurant.' The meaning hinges on 'head chef' working together with 'restaurant' in spoken Russian.
'To whom I owe everything.' Notice how Russian expresses 'whom' and 'to everyone' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Which is why I consider him a genius.' Vika anchors the line on 'why', while 'genius' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Well, that is a rather strange taste, right?' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'yes' without extra filler words.
'Maybe it is because of the prunes?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'maybe' before landing on 'prunes'.
'It is pure vinegar.' The grammar packs 'continuous' and 'vinegar' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Vika answers right away.
Дорогие друзья, к сожалению, мне пора в аэропорт.
'Dear friends, unfortunately it is time for me to head to the airport.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'dear' and finishing on 'the airport'.
'Viktor Petrovich.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'Viktor' and 'Petrovich' in a few short words.
'Here are the keys to my.' The meaning hinges on 'there you go' working together with 'my' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'New car.' Notice how Russian expresses 'new' and 'cars' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Господа, хочу сказать буквально пару слов.
Это блюдо в свое время придумал мой учитель.
Дорогие друзья, к сожалению, мне пора в аэропорт.

That wraps up this scene as before the guests taste the roll, Barani publicly credits Viktor Petrovich Barinov as the true creator of the dish and gifts him a brand-new car, right as the vinegar ruins the tasting. See you next time!
